summary:
Every acceptance criterion I could reach holds on this PC (Windows 11 26200, not elevated, TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP as the engine runs it).

**Full suite**
- Engine's TEMP: 789/789 passed, exit 0.
- User's TEMP: 789/789 passed, exit 0, both when set through `dotnet test -e` and when set in the shell.
- The three formerly red tests pass in both runs.

**The Windows-folder tests**
- They run in the default suite: the default-filter run lists all five.
- Nested tree in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests: kept 4 of 7, 4 still old, moved root, plain and links. Same result for the as-is, lower-case and trailing-separator root spellings.
- Refusing child: kept 1 of 2, 1 still old.
- Outside the Windows folder: 7/7/7.

**Two mutations of the counter correction, each restored with git checkout and a fresh timestamp**
- (A) With the decrement removed, the three nested-tree rows fail with "(asked, kept) = (7, 7), but 4 ... Kept over-counts", and the SL-096 bug test fails too.
- (B) The attempted-open rule the spike rejected (count a parent out whether the child's open succeeded or not) fails the refusing-child test, kept 0 against 1 still old. This settles O-014.
- After restoring, the Debug and Release Core DLLs and the published exe all contain the correction, and the five tests pass again.

**Rules and app**
- Fitness: all 87 rules hold.
- eng/rules-harness/harness.py, run under the engine's interpreter against taad_v3 6236270 (Q-027, because this slice changes .taad/fitness.yaml): 117/117 AS-RECORDED, exit 0. One import rule was not run because the scratch copy has no code graph; this is known.
- RuleCases C-001: AGREE, 18 facts, 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns, 65 settled.
- A real single-file publish (139,951,256 B) scanned C:\Windows\Web through eng/read-window.ps1: outcome completed, 0 unreadable, exit 0.

**Leftovers**
- C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests holds 0 entries afterwards.
- The user's fsa-tests holds only the 4 folders from 24 and 27 Sep.
- No testhost processes are left.

**O-015 cannot be checked here.** There is no Windows 10 machine, and writing test folders under %ProgramData% or %ProgramFiles% is outside what I may touch. The ScanResult contract (ScanResult.cs:203) and the triage doc (lines 89-90) record both as unmeasured and uncorrected, and Q-205 accepts Windows 10 as unverified.

The bug report itself carried only its title. I assumed it means exactly what the investigation reproduced. Contact is graded `code`: the evidence is test runs, even though those tests act on the real C:\Windows\Temp and the real luafv driver.

criteria.criterion: 1. Count kept folders: a nested 7-folder tree under %SystemRoot%\Temp, back-dated deepest-first, where root, plain and links each have two child folders
criteria.how: LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests Theory, as-is row, under C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests: 'kept 4 of 7; 4 of 7 folders still at least 47 h old; moved: <root>, plain, links'. Same in 4 separate runs (engine TEMP, user TEMP, default filter, after restore).

criteria.criterion: 2. Count kept folders: a kept folder whose only child folder refuses FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, under %SystemRoot%\Temp
criteria.how: AChildThatRefusesWriteAttributesLeavesItsParentCountedAsKept: 'kept 1 of 2; 1 of 2 still old; moved: none'. Mutation B (the attempted-open rule) makes it fail with kept 0 vs 1, so the test pins the successful-keep-open rule.

criteria.criterion: 3. Count kept folders: scan root spelled in lower case
criteria.how: Theory lower-case row scans c:\windows\temp\fsa-tests\<guid>: kept 4 of 7, 4 still old. Under mutation A it fails with kept 7 vs 4.

criteria.criterion: 4. Count kept folders: scan root with a trailing backslash
criteria.how: Theory trailing-separator row (…\<guid>\): kept 4 of 7, 4 still old. As critique m5 accepted, this is a spelling check only: Scan trims the separator first.

criteria.how: OutsideTheWindowsFolderEveryKeptFolderStaysKept, under C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-tests: kept 7 of 7, 7 still old, nothing moved. Passes under both mutations, so the correction does not reach outside the Windows folder.

criteria.how: TempTreeRootTests.ARedirectTargetThatIsNotOutsideTheWindowsFolderIsRefusedByName passed: the refusal is named. Pure function only; not run as SYSTEM or a service account.

criteria.how: InTree asserts the tree is gone after Dispose. The refusing-child test (deny ACE) passed in every run. C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests listed 0 entries after about 6 runs of the tests, mutants included. The bug test's own trees, direct children of C:\Windows\Temp, cannot be listed (see not_reached).

criteria.criterion: 12. Keep an over-reporting regression visible in the routine suite when the Scanner correction is reverted
criteria.how: Mutation A (decrement removed): all three Theory rows fail with '(asked, kept) = (7, 7), but 4 ... Kept over-counts'. The default-filter run shows these tests in the routine suite. Fitness rule 1 and TheWindowsFolderFactsRunInTheDefaultSuite hold.

criteria.criterion: 13. Back-date a fixture before judging the scan: HeldOpenTreeTests/LastAccessTests trees in %SystemRoot%\Temp after the deepest-first reorder
criteria.how: The reorder is in the diff (children before parents in both fixtures). The design owes no new test; spike 2 measured that failures move from the preconditions (:68/:96) to the scan assertions (:78/:87). With the redirect, both classes pass under both TEMPs. I did not place these two classes in C:\Windows\Temp myself.

criteria.criterion: 14. Count kept folders: a folder never asked (SMB, cloud placeholder or sync root, excluded store) or a cancelled scan
criteria.how: By reading the code, not by running it. The correction sits behind `asked` and io.KeptLastAccess, so it adds no branch for never-asked folders, and cancelled counters stay partial as before. The design owes no new test. The existing gate tests pass in the 789.

obligations.evidence: Measured under C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests with tree (d): R\refusing\x.bin, with a deny FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES ACE on refusing. The shipped successful-keep-open rule gives 'kept 1 of 2; 1 of 2 folders still at least 47 h old; moved: none', so kept 1 equals the truth of 1. This held in 4 runs. As a contrast, I swapped in the attempted-open rule (a mutation of Scanner.cs, since restored): the same test fails with 'kept 0 of 2; 1 of 2 still old'. This reproduces spike 1's no-go, and shows the shipped rule is the one that matches.

Not measurable on this PC by this stage, for three reasons. There is no Windows 10 machine (Q-205 keeps Windows 10 supported but unverified). Creating test folders in %ProgramData% means writing outside this tree, which is the person's call. %ProgramFiles% needs an administrator. Neither offered admin operation measures it. Only C:\Windows\Temp on Windows 11 26200 was measured. ScanResult.cs:203 and docs/design/SL-096-last-access-under-windows-temp.md:89-90 record ProgramData/ProgramFiles as unmeasured and uncorrected, and Windows 10 as unmeasured. A person runs this: (a) On Windows 10: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests|FullyQualifiedName~LastAccessTests|FullyQualifiedName~HeldOpenTreeTests"`. All must pass, and the Theory must print 'kept 4 of 7 ... moved: <root>, plain, links'. If it prints 'kept 4 of 7; 7 of 7 still old', luafv does not act there and the correction under-counts. (b) In a writable folder under C:\ProgramData: build R\S, back-date S and then R by 48 h, open S with FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, and read R's last access. If it moved to now, WindowsFolderFromEnvironment's location list needs widening.

not_reached: Windows 10: neither LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests nor the 23 last-access tests were run there (no machine; Q-205). If luafv does not move parents there, the kept == still-old tests would go red, because the correction would count out parents that never moved.

%ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%: whether a child's write-class open moves its parent there is unmeasured. Measuring it means writing outside this tree, or an administrator. The correction covers %SystemRoot% only.
Whether luafv.sys itself issues the parent query: it needs fltmc or a trace as an administrator. Neither offered operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) can do it, so I did not ask for one.

Whether the bug test's two runs during my mutations left C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096-<guid> trees behind. C:\Windows\Temp cannot be listed by this user. The test deletes with Directory.Delete, which the survey showed works there, but nothing confirms it. The survey's earlier leftover (fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex>) and the code review's probable C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-parity-case-<10 hex> also still need an administrator to remove them.
The opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT, Network=SMB-LOOPBACK and Network=TEST-NET-1 tests were not run. The default filter excludes them, and SyncRootRig is not yet routed through TempTree; that is filed.

The app shows no last-access counters (Q-103/Q-159). The real publish run therefore shows only that the shipped exe still scans a Windows-folder root to completion, not the corrected count in the app.
The design's TempTree root-choice branches for a SYSTEM or service profile were exercised only as a pure function, not by running the suite as LocalSystem or a service account.
